pairs: Fili mi,
My son,
custodi sermones meos, et præcepta mea reconde tibi. Fili,
guard my words and conceal my precepts within you.
serva mandata mea,
Son, preserve my commandments,
et vives; et legem meam quasi pupillam oculi tui:
and you shall live. And keep my law as the pupil of your eye.
liga eam in digitis tuis,
Bind it with your fingers;
scribe illam in tabulis cordis tui.
write it on the tablets of your heart.
Dic sapientiæ:
Say to wisdom,
Soror mea es,
“You are my sister,”
et prudentiam voca amicam tuam:
and call prudence your friend.
ut custodiant te a muliere extranea,
So may she guard you from the woman who is an outsider,
et ab aliena quæ verba sua dulcia facit.
and from the stranger who sweetens her words.
De fenestra enim domus meæ per cancellos prospexi,
For I gaze from the window of my house, through the lattice,
et video parvulos;
and I see little ones.
considero vecordem juvenem,
I consider a frenzied youth,
qui transit per plateam juxta angulum et prope viam domus illius graditur:
who crosses the street at the corner and close to the way of that house.
in obscuro,
He steps into shadows,
advesperascente die,
as day becomes evening,
in noctis tenebris et caligine.
into the darkness and gloom of the night.
Et ecce occurrit illi mulier ornatu meretricio,
And behold, a woman meets him, dressed like a harlot,
præparata ad capiendas animas: garrula et vaga,
prepared to captivate souls: chattering and rambling,
quietis impatiens,
unwilling to bear silence,
nec valens in domo consistere pedibus suis;
unable to keep her feet at home,
nunc foris,
now outside,
nunc in plateis,
now in the streets,
nunc juxta angulos insidians.
now lying in ambush near the corners.
Apprehensumque deosculatur juvenem,
And overtaking the youth, she kisses him,
et procaci vultu blanditur,
and with a provocative face, she flatters him,
dicens:
saying:
Victimas pro salute vovi;
“I vowed sacrifices for well-being.
hodie reddidi vota mea:
Today I have repaid my vows.
idcirco egressa sum in occursum tuum,
Because of this, I have gone out to meet you,
desiderans te videre, et reperi.
desiring to see you, and I have found you.
Intexui funibus lectulum meum;
I have woven my bed with cords.
stravi tapetibus pictis ex Ægypto:
I have strewn it with embroidered tapestries from Egypt.
aspersi cubile meum myrrha,
I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh,
et aloë,
aloe,
et cinnamomo.
and cinnamon.
Veni, inebriemur uberibus,
Come, let us be inebriated in abundance,
et fruamur cupitis amplexibus donec illucescat dies.
and let us delight in the embraces of desire, until the day begins to dawn.
Non est enim vir in domo sua:
For my husband is not in his house.
abiit via longissima:
He has gone away on a very long journey.
sacculum pecuniæ secum tulit;
He took with him a bag of money.
in die plenæ lunæ reversurus est in domum suam.
He will return to his house on the day of the full moon.”
Irretivit eum multis sermonibus,
She enmeshed him with many words,
et blanditiis labiorum protraxit illum.
and she drew him forward with the flattery of her lips.
Statim eam sequitur quasi bos ductus ad victimam,
Immediately, he follows her, like an ox being led to the sacrifice,
et quasi agnus lasciviens,
and like a lamb acting lasciviously,
et ignorans quod ad vincula stultus trahatur:
and not knowing that he is being drawn foolishly into chains,
donec transfigat sagitta jecur ejus,
until the arrow pierces his liver.
velut si avis festinet ad laqueum,
It is just as if a bird were to hurry into the snare.
et nescit quod de periculo animæ illius agitur.
And he does not know that his actions endanger his own soul.
Nunc ergo,
Therefore,
fili mi,
my son,
audi me,
hear me now,
et attende verbis oris mei.
and attend to the words of my mouth.
Ne abstrahatur in viis illius mens tua,
Do not let your mind be pulled into her ways.
neque decipiaris semitis ejus;
And do not be deceived by her paths.
multos enim vulneratos dejecit,
For she has tossed aside many wounded,
et fortissimi quique interfecti sunt ab ea.
and some of those who were very strong have been slain by her.
Viæ inferi domus ejus,
Her household is the way to Hell,
penetrantes in interiora mortis.
reaching even to the inner places of death.
